name: comp-362

frames.best_why: Tooltip is open with date plus three labelled value rows, all fully readable above the button.

tagline: A hover popup breaks a day into coloured dots, labels and dollar amounts.
summary: A small outlined Chart button opens a compact tooltip on hover. The tooltip shows a date heading and three rows, each pairing a coloured dot and a metric name with a right-aligned value.
appearance: At rest a small outlined Chart button sits centred in a bordered card with a caption beneath. Hovering opens a light tooltip above it: a bold date heading, then three rows each with a coloured dot, a label and a right-aligned dollar value.
behaviour: Hovering or focusing the Chart button opens the tooltip immediately, and moving away dismisses it. The tooltip only appears and disappears; its values never change.
demo_content: Chart button in a card captioned 'Hover for a chart-style breakdown.' with tooltip Sales $40, Revenue $74, Costs $410.
search_phrases: hover popup with a breakdown of numbers
tooltip showing chart values for a day
small popup with coloured dots and amounts
hover over a button to see sales revenue costs
date and metric breakdown on hover
tooltip with key and value pairs
use_when: A compact control needs to reveal a small dated breakdown of figures without opening a full chart.
avoid_when: The values and date are fixed inside the tooltip, so real data needs code changes.
customise: The date, metric labels, values and dot colours are written directly in the tooltip, so real data means editing the source; the trigger label is fixed too.
weight_why: One button and a small popup with three rows; no chart engine or loop.

a11y.note: The tooltip opens on focus and is linked by the tooltip primitive, but each dot carries meaning only through colour.

issues: Data is hardcoded to one date and three metrics; it does not follow a real dataset.
Colour is the only cue tying each dot to a series.
polish_why: Neat compact tooltip; the plain demo card and fixed data make it ordinary.
